  2. Library Journal Star Libraries

City Librarian McDermott highlighted that the Crowell Public Library was ranked in the top 5%

  3. Joint Meeting for all Library Support Groups

Chairperson Mollno emphasized the value of hosting a Joint Meeting with the Library, the San

  4. Library as a Vote Center on February 29 – March 3, 2020

City Librarian McDermott reported that the Barth Community Room in the Crowell Public
Library was designated as a Voting Center for the California Primary Elections to occur from
February 29 – March 3, 2020.

  5. Census at the Library

City Librarian McDermott reported that the Library will aid in the United State Census and will
designate several public-access computers towards that purpose.

  6. Grant Proposal to Refurbish the Young Adult Area

City Librarian McDermott proposed applying for a grant the fund the refurbishment of the Young
Adult area in the Crowell Public Library.

and updated cost were not readily available. A pre-bid meeting was held for the Barth Room AV
upgrades and staff are waiting on the bids for the project. For Fiscal Year 2020-21, window tinting,

SUBJECT:  CITY LIBRARIAN’S UPDATE REPORT FOR JUNE 2020

BACKGROUND

At the request of the Library Board of Trustees, the City Librarian provides a monthly update of
the operations of the Crowell Public Library of the City of San Marino. The update report
provides relevant statistics and information to allow the Board to have a macro view of the
Library.

DISCUSSION

Since the last Trustee meeting of February 24, 2020, the library has undergone a profound service
model. The library was closed to the public on March 17, 2020. A program of curbside circulation
was implemented. In May, it was decided to begin accepting contactless book returns in the book
drops.

The U.S. Department of State has not reopened to process passports.

In order to perform critical work on the electrical system in our area, a contractor for Edison
will cut the power to the library on Wednesday, June 24. A generator will be supplied, so library
operations should suffer little downtime.

Friends of the Library

The Friends of the Library have not met since the closing on March 18. They will have a meeting
on Thursday, June 25, to discuss their plans for the new fiscal year. They have not given us their
final donation for this fiscal year. It is unknown how their reduced income will affect their gift to
us in FY 20-21. Their traditional gift has been $50,000, which pays mainly for children’s books
and programs.

San Marino Public Library Foundation

  13
 The San Marino Public Library Foundation has not met since the library’s closure to the public.
They gave the library $2000 to buy eBooks through Overdrive Advantage, which will be
exclusively available to Crowell Library card holder.

Operations

The Librarian 1 p-t position, which has been open since last August, has been re-posted.

The Adult Reference Librarian is preparing for her maternity leave starting at the end of July. If
we re-open during her leave with limited hours, we will have enough full and part-time personnel
to cover the reference desk. If more coverage is needed, we can bring in a substitute reference
librarian.

Statistics

Statistics for the last three months show that, due to COVID-19, our print circulation has fallen.
Conversely, our e-Book circulation has risen considerably as has our Flipster e-magazine service.
Our curbside pickup service was very popular when we first offered it. Activity slowed for two
months afterward. Recently, it has surged again. Curbside requests are highest at the beginning
of the week.

Programming and Services

Adult virtual programs have seen robust attendance, averaging 30 attendees each.

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the Library Board of Trustees receive and file this information report.

SUBJECT:  MANAGEMENT ANALYST’S UPDATE REPORT FOR JUNE 2020

BACKGROUND

At the request of the Library Board of Trustees, the Management Analyst provides a monthly
update of the financial condition of the Crowell Public Library of the City of San Marino. The
update report provides relevant information to allow the Board to have a macro view of the fiscal
health of the Library. In addition, the report includes information about projects funded through
the Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) and other major assignments managed by the Management
Analyst.

DISCUSSION

On March 17, 2020 the City of San Marino ordered all non-essential city activities to cease
operation due to COVID-19. This order greatly impacted the Community Services Department.
The City’s order also directed that the Crowell Public Library not permit public access into the
facility thereby further impacting the Library’s operations.

FY 19-20 Budget Update

Due to the City’s COVID-19 order, the Library was underspent in several accounting areas as
the Library was unable to offer its traditional programming and services. This will result in savings
that will return to the City’s reserve at the end of Fiscal Year 2019-2020 which ends after June
30, 2020. As the Board is aware, a financial update has not been provided since February 2020 as
a result of the City’s cancellations of non-essential meetings, events, and activities. Therefore, the
following is a high-level summary of the major developments that occurred since the last update
report.

On January 31, 2020, the City Council signed the new Memorandums of Understanding (MOU)
with the City’s Police Officers’ Association, Firefighters’ Association, and City Employees’

  32
 Association bargaining units. The MOU’s reflected an effective date of July 1, 2019. As a result,
affected employees received a salary adjustment in February 2020. In March 2020, affected
employees received health premium refunds and retroactive payments for salary pay for the
period from July 1, 2019 through February 1, 2020. Therefore, larger personnel expenditures are
reflected in March because of this activity.

Several part-time staff chose to not return to work or were unable to work because of COVID-
19. In addition, the City directed full-time staff to reduce their work hours to allow for physical
distancing in the workplace or because of a reduction in services. Full-time staff who worked at
least 53 hours in a pay period continued to receive their full salary. Full-time staff who worked
at least 27 hours but less than 53 hours received two-thirds of their salary and three staff
members in the Library fell into this category. All full-time staff continued to receive their full
benefits. As a result, the Library will see savings in personnel-related expenditures.

In April 2020, the City received the generous donation of $36,000 from the San Marino Public
Library Foundation to use towards the upgrade of the 36 public-access computers. The City will
have to pay an additional cost of $1,660.08 for an unforeseen software upgrade.

A total of $18,894.55 in expenditures were miscoded throughout the fiscal year. From that total,
$215.61 were charges made to accounts that did not have budgeted monies. Staff noted the
errors and make the appropriate corrections.

Furthermore, the closure of the Crowell Public Library stopped the flow of revenues to the City.
The Library is projected to close the fiscal year with $202,713.70 or 63% of the total of estimated
General Fund revenues. Passports accounted for 80.9% of all the revenues collected by the
Library, which amounted to $164,086.02. Donations were still collected and $13,300 was donated
to the Library (not including the $36,000 from the Foundation) since the closure of the Library.
As of June 10, 2020, the Library received 71% of the total amount of donations that were
projected to be received in FY 2019-20.

The attached Budget Monitor shows expenses and revenues as of June 10, 2020 when the latest
Demand Register was submitted to Council.

Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) Projects

As stated earlier, the City is moving forward with the upgrade of the 36 public-access computers.
The procurement of the computers was delayed due to the fluctuations of pricing that resulted
from uncertainties in electronics supply chains. However, we recently saw pricing stabilize as
economies began to reopen and we finalized the Purchase Order for the machines on June 1,
2020. The upgrade is projected to be completed at the end of July 2020.

    NOTE: Upgrades to staff computers are being handled by the City’s Finance Department
  and are funded through the City’s Capital Improvement Plan. Four library staff computers

   were replaced in FY 2019-2020. 18 library staff computers are slated to be replaced in FY
  2020-2021.

The Barth Room Audio/Visual upgrade was put on hold on March 25, 2020 as a result of the City
not receiving enough bids. Parks and Public Works Director Michael Throne advised that the
project will be incorporated in future improvements. No additional updates are available at this
time.

In addition, the County of Los Angeles ordered countless businesses to cease operations to
control the spread of COVID-19. This order impacted the contractor who was working on the
installation of the Library awning and the contractor is expected to resume work on the awning
as soon as possible. Parks and Public Works staff advised that the contractor is expected to
complete work by June 30, 2020.

Other Items

None

SUBJECT:  UPDATE ON CROWELL PUBLIC LIBRARY’S RESPONSE TO
  COVID-19

BACKGROUND

An outbreak of respiratory illness due to a novel coronavirus, now known as COVID-19, was
identified in Wuhan City, China in December 2019. Symptoms of the virus include fever, cough,
and shortness of breath, and infected individuals have experienced a range of outcomes, from
mild sickness to severe illness and death. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
(“CDC”) believes that symptoms appear within two to fourteen days after exposure. Currently,
there is no vaccine to prevent COVID-19.

The CDC’s guidance to manage ongoing COVID-19 risk requires extraordinary efforts, including
limiting public gatherings. On March 17, 2020, the City Council proclaimed a local emergency
due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The federal government, State of California, Los Angeles County
Board of Supervisors, and the Los Angeles County Health Officer have also taken action to
declare public health emergencies. On March 19, 2020, both the County and State issued “Stay
at Home” orders.

The City of San Marino cancelled all non-essential city-sponsored meetings and ordered the
closure of or limited access to public facilities, including the Crowell Public Library. The initial
closures were set to last until March 31, 2020 but were extended multiple times. Currently, the
closures are set to expire after June 30, 2020.

DISCUSSION

In response to the COVID 19 threat, the library closed to the public on March 18, 2020. Soon
afterward, the library began a program of “curbside pickup”, in which patrons called in to ask for
books. When they come to the library, the books were delivered to the trunks of their cars,

  36
 making the delivery “contactless”. This service is offered Monday through Friday from 11 a.m. to
4 p.m.

Operations

In order to minimize workplace contacts, staff schedules were reduced and staggered. Reference
librarians were reduced to 20 hours per week. Nevertheless, book circulation is robust. We
began to accept returns. These are “quarantined”, placed on a table in the Life Long Learning
center for 72 hours to eliminate any possible contamination upon re-shelving.

Programming and Services

Programming was adapted to be virtual. For example, Family story time is offered over Facebook.
The Summer Reading Club will run as a virtual program over Beanstack. That program begins on
June 22. Here is the library’s virtual program schedule:

    Adult Library Assistant takes tech questions over the phone Mondays and Wednesdays,
  11-4.
    Adult Library Assistant is making video guides to our electronic resources.
    Monday at 11: Adult Reference Librarian conducts Stir Crazy book talk on Facebook
    Monday at 2: Virtual Coffee, Tea and Chat in Mandarin on Zoom
    Wednesday: “Quarantine Art Gallery” for teens
    Thursday at 11: Family Story Time on Facebook
    Thursday afternoon: Virtual Lego “Quest”

Reopening

Staff will return to their regular schedules on June 29. To date the city has not received specific
direction from the county regarding the date to re-open libraries. We anticipate that information
will be coming in the very near future.

When the library does re-open, it will be with limited hours and metered entry. Patrons will
enter the library through the Barth Community Room. There, staff check for face coverings and
apply hand sanitizer. Twelve individual patrons or group of household members will be allowed
in the library at one time. They will be given a book basket to use in the library. After they check
out, the basket will be sanitized and returned to the Barth Room for the next patron or family
group.

Patrons will exit out of the library front door.

The library will be open to the public from 11 a.m. – 4 p.m. Monday through Friday. 11 a.m. –
12 p.m. will be “Senior Hour” open to those 60 or older.

Floor decals at 6-foot intervals identify the line for patrons at the circulation desk.

The gate between the Circulation Desk and the Barth Room will be dropped.

  2
  37
 Employees, wearing face coverings and gloves, are positioned 6 feet from each other and from
patrons to check out books or to answer reference questions.

The library will continue its contactless return system (e.g., patrons drop them into library drop
boxes or during regular hours in bins outside the library). Returned items are isolated and
remain untouched for at least three days before handling and re-shelving.

Public internet access computers will not be available, nor will the Dakim Brain Fitness not the
AWE computers. Access to the public copier will not be available. Most chairs will be removed
from the public area.

Public service desks have plastic barriers installed to limit contact between employees and
patrons.

Public service desks will be wiped down hourly as will ball-point pens available to the public.

Visitors and tenants are instructed that they must wear cloth face coverings while in the
building when in contact when other people. This applies to all adults and to children over the
age of 2. Only individuals with chronic respiratory conditions or other medical conditions that
make use of a mask hazardous are exempted from this requirement.

Visitors and tenants arriving at the building with children must ensure that their children stay
next to a parent, avoid touching any other person or any item that does not belong to them,
and are masked if age permits.

The single bathrooms will be available to the public upon request. The lobby restrooms will be
locked.

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the Library Board of Trustees receive and file this information report.

ATTACHMENTS

None
